prerequisites: Knowledge of phisical metallurgy of plastic deformation and fracture and of the strengthening methods of metallic materials

learning_outcomes.text: Educate students on the main classes of metallic materials and the technologies that can contribute to sustainable mobility.

Knowledge of the characteristics of high-strength steels; aluminum, magnesium, and titanium alloys for structural lightweighting; permanent magnets and rare earths; lithium, cobalt, nickel, and manganese for batteries; and catalysts for hydrogen production and fuel cells, their production technologies, and their sustainability.
Understand the operating mechanisms, advantages, and disadvantages of additive manufacturing applications in product optimization.

syllabus_topics: Light alloys: aluminum, magnesium, and titanium
Batteries and lithium, cobalt, nickel, and manganese
Hydrogen, electrolysis and catalysts, fuel cells
teaching_methods: In-depth analysis of topics through scientific literature
assessment_rules: An oral exam and a student seminar will be graded. The final grade will be calculated by averaging the two grades.
